subject: [PATCH v6 05/25] btrfs: zoned: use the regular allocator for conventional metadata block groups

reviews.author: Johannes Thumshirn
reviews.summary: reviewer noted that the current implementation of dev replace can lead to illegal allocations when replacing a device from conventional zones to sequential zones, and suggested creating a fstest to catch this issue
reviews.raw_body:
Oh now I get it. But with that patch set that shouldn't happen anymore 
or at least be way less likely. I agree we need to do something against 
it though. I guess we can make a fstest to catch it: fill the metadata 
by creating a ton of inline extents until we have used up all 
conventional zones and, more to have sth on a sequential zone and then 
do a dev-replace.

I'll try to cook up something.

2026-11-10.patch_summary: This patch addresses an issue where replacing a device in a Btrfs filesystem could lead to illegal allocations due to the BLOCK_GROUP_FLAG_SEQUENTIAL_ZONE flag not being updated correctly. The problem arises when a block group is created on a device with conventional zones and then replaced with a device having sequential zones, causing the system to hang or allocate blocks incorrectly. To fix this, the patch likely updates the allocator to handle such replacements more robustly.
